caption: Psalm 22 and Jesus’s final prayer share trust in mortal danger. But ‘Into Your hands I commit My Spirit’ directly quotes Psalm 31—not Psalm 22.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s final prayer? Psalm 22 asks God to rescue the sufferer. Luke says Jesus entrusted his spirit to the Father before dying.
slides.body: Psalm 22 asks God to rescue the sufferer. Luke says Jesus entrusted his spirit to the Father before dying.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict Jesus’s final prayer?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:20-21: Deliver my soul from the sword … Save me from the mouth of the lion.
slides.body: Deliver my soul from the sword … Save me from the mouth of the lion.
slides.heading: Ps 22:20-21

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Lk 23:46, BSB: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
slides.body: Then Jesus called out in a loud voice, “Father, into Your hands I commit My Spirit.” And when He had said this, He breathed His last.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Lk 23:46

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Both passages show trust Each speaker turns to God in mortal danger. That makes the comparison understandable.
slides.body: Each speaker turns to God in mortal danger. That makes the comparison understandable.
slides.heading: Both passages show trust

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But Luke quotes another psalm ‘Into Your hands I commit My Spirit’ comes from Psalm 31:5. Those words are not in Psalm 22.
